items.title: Technical Product Manager, GRC Systems
items.description: About the Team OpenAI's Governance, Risk, and Compliance team works within Security to connect obligations and customer commitments to effective controls and reliable evidence. We partner across the organization to make security easier to put into practice and easier to understand. About the Role We are hiring a Technical Product Manager to own the vision and build the systems behind GRC and Security. You will discover what users need, decide what to build and sequence first, and personally implement data models, integrations, and working workflows. You will carry those products through testing, adoption, and operation. Much of this work is a data problem: understanding what exists, how it changes, which information can be trusted, and what should happen next. You will apply product design and solution architecture to make security controls part of everyday work and produce reliable evidence through their operation. That evidence should support organizational excellence, audits, customers, and regulatory needs and help our audience understand and use the security information relevant to them. You should be comfortable moving between implementation detail and consequential decisions. You may spend one part of the day debugging a data flow and another explaining the architecture, evidence, and tradeoffs to leadership or an external audience. You will begin as a hands-on individual contributor, setting direction and helping colleagues build effectively. In this role, you will: - Own the product vision and technical direction for an agreed portfolio of GRC systems, discovering user needs and deciding what to build and sequence first. - Design and build scalable data models, integrations, and workflows that connect requirements, systems, people, controls, actions, and evidence. - Establish data quality, ownership, history, and freshness practices so changes and missing information produce accurate, useful behavior. - Build approved security requirements into usable workflows, automate appropriate checks and actions, and verify that controls operate as intended with the teams that own them. - Create clear employee experiences that reduce duplicate requests and make the secure path easy to complete. - Develop evidence capabilities for auditors, regulators, and customers, including understandable views and structured outputs with appropriate access, scope, and disclosure boundaries. - Carry work through testing, release, adoption, monitoring, and maintenance; improve the system when scale or new requirements expose weaknesses. - Explain architecture, security outcomes, evidence, and tradeoffs to technical teams and senior or external audiences; create reusable patterns that help others deliver independently. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have personally designed, built, and scaled products or operational systems and can explain the decisions, failures, and outcomes you owned. - Can still build and troubleshoot data models, queries, integrations, or workflows, even if your current role is not software engineering. - Understand how data identity, relationships, quality, history, and access affect the correctness of a system and its outputs. - Can turn an ambiguous need into a product direction, buildable requirements, a practical first release, and evidence that people benefit from it. - Understand security controls and assurance well enough to connect a requirement to implementation, operating evidence, and an appropriately scoped claim; deepen domain knowledge with experts where needed. - Communicate complex systems and risk clearly to engineers, executives, and external audiences, preserving the facts and limitations. - Take responsibility through operation, learn from feedback, and help others own and extend your work. Relevant backgrounds include engineering, data architecture, technical product ownership, internal systems, and security or compliance engineering. Prior engineering experience is valuable; a current engineering title, specific degree, certification, management history, or experience with our tools is not required. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. items.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. THE TEAM Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. This role sits within SOX Compliance and is the senior technical authority for IT controls in the SOX program. You will set the strategy for ITGCs, IT application controls, and the controls over private key management and digital asset custody. Internal Audit independently tests the controls you own. You will own the ITGC SOX program, building the control framework, testing approach, and evidence standards from the ground up. This is a hands-on role with real program ownership at a crypto exchange. The technology stack spans blockchain-native infrastructure, digital asset custody systems, and on-chain and off-chain processing, and engineering changes at a pace most companies never see. The systems are complex, the deployments are frequent, and the controls are consequential. THE OPPORTUNITY - Strategy & program ownership - Own the enterprise IT SOX strategy and roadmap, covering ITGC, ITAC, and digital asset and key management controls across all in-scope entities and jurisdictions. - Define the scoping methodology and risk assessment for IT SOX, including in-scope applications, infrastructure, wallet and custody systems, and third-party and service-organization dependencies. - Set control design standards and own the control framework. Design controls that fit modern engineering practices (CI/CD, infrastructure as code, cloud) and don’t slow them down. - Set the standard for management testing and evidence. Direct co-sourced and matrixed resources, and review the quality of their work. - Use AI-enabled workflows, continuous controls monitoring, and data analytics to move IT SOX from periodic testing toward scalable, automated assurance. Private key management & digital asset controls - Own SOX control design and coverage for the full private key lifecycle: generation, storage, access, signing and approval workflows, rotation, backup and recovery, and retirement. - Assess controls over key custody architectures, such as HSMs, MPC, multi-signature, and hot/warm/cold wallet structures, including segregation of duties, quorum and approval controls, and privileged access. - Evaluate how key management and custody controls support the existence, completeness, and safeguarding of customer and corporate digital assets and their financial reporting implications. - Assess controls over on-chain and off-chain transaction processing, reconciliation of wallets to ledgers, and reliance on blockchain data and third-party custodians or service organizations. - Be the SOX authority on emerging digital asset risks and decide how the control framework should respond as products, chains, and custody models evolve. Deficiency evaluation & remediation - Lead evaluation of control deficiencies, including root cause analysis and severity and pervasiveness assessments, and recommend classification (control deficiency, significant deficiency, or material weakness). - Own remediation strategy for open ITGC and key management findings. Drive executive-level accountability with Engineering, Security, and Infrastructure leaders. - Escalate gaps and delays directly to senior leadership. Report status to the Audit Committee as required. - Coordinate with Internal Audit so remediated controls are ready for independent validation. Executive & external stakeholder engagement - Be the senior SOX voice to the CFO, CISO, CTO, Controller, and the Audit Committee on IT control posture, risks, and remediation. - Lead the external auditor relationship on IT matters: audit strategy, reliance and scoping decisions, walkthroughs, and resolution of disagreements. - Serve as a trusted advisor to engineering and security leaders, translating audit and control requirements into practical engineering decisions. - Partner with Internal Audit, ERM, the business process SOX lead, and co-sourced providers to align coverage across the full assurance program. - Mentor SOX and risk team members and raise the technical bar across the function. WHAT YOU BRING - 10+ years in SOX compliance, IT audit, internal audit, or external audit, with deep ITGC experience and a record of owning programs at enterprise scale. - Direct, hands-on experience with crypto and private key management controls, including designing, assessing, or auditing controls over key custody, wallet infrastructure, signing, and digital asset safeguarding. This is a must-have. - Experience in a crypto exchange, custodian, fintech, or payments company with complex, rapidly evolving infrastructure. - CISA and CPA certifications required. Candidates with one who are actively pursuing the other will be considered. - Expert knowledge of ITGC frameworks, SOX 404, COSO, COBIT, and PCAOB standards, with the judgment to make and defend scoping, reliance, and deficiency-classification decisions. - Strong technical fluency in how systems, databases, cloud infrastructure, and deployment pipelines work. - Proven ability to connect an ITGC or key management failure to its impact on business process controls and the financial statements. - Experience working with external auditors (Big 4 preferred) and presenting to Audit Committees and senior executives. - Experience across multi-entity structures or multiple jurisdictions. - Exceptional communicator who earns credibility with both engineers and finance executives. NICE TO HAVES - Experience building or scaling an IT SOX program in a growth-stage or first-year SOX company. - Familiarity with CI/CD, GitLab or similar version control, and cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP). - Familiarity with SOC 1/SOC 2 reliance for custodians and service providers, and with proof-of-reserves or similar attestations. - Familiarity with audit and GRC platforms such as AuditBoard or Workiva. - Familiarity with AI-assisted compliance tools and willingness to adopt new technologies. Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. OUR COMMITMENT Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto. We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision. As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. items.title: Compliance Officer and Deputy MLRO
items.description: Based in the heart of Manchester, Betable Group are a team with knowledge and dedication to both online gaming and fintech solutions. We are responsible for delivering top-class online gaming experiences for customers of over 100 online casino and bingo sites both in Great Britain and internationally. Betable also have our own cutting-edge iGaming platform which hosts an array of casinos which enables them to operate as well as an exciting new payment solution which handles high volumes of payment transactions. The Compliance Officer & DMLRO plays a pivotal role in ensuring regulatory compliance, operational alignment, and adherence to licensing obligations across our operations in both Great Britain and internationally. This position would be well suited to an accomplished AML professional looking to expand into a more generalist compliance role. The role will also be central to driving capability, innovation and accountability of our regulatory reporting, people and systems. Led by the Compliance Manager & MLRO, the successful candidate will contribute to the design and execution of the company’s remote games testing strategy. They will lead the delivery of key projects supporting the wider compliance team and protecting the Group’s interests at all times. In addition to these responsibilities, the postholder will perform the role of DMLRO for the both GB licences, along with any further international licences obtained in future, supported by nominated officers and under the guidance of the MLRO. Finally, the postholder will maintain all relevant Games Registers both internally and externally with regulators, ensuring this process is fit for purpose and audited regularly. For candidates based in, or within a commutable distance of our Manchester office, we operate a hybrid working model with a minimum of two days per week in the office. Some occasional travel may be required to attend audits, conferences, training sessions, or other business needs as they arise. We are seeking a driven, experienced, and forward-thinking compliance professional. This is a significant opportunity to shape the compliance function locally while contributing to broader group initiatives. It is ideally suited to an ambitious individual looking to expand their remit and play a key role in the next phase of our growth. • Work alongside the MLRO to ensure the group maintains a fit-for-purpose Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Counter-Terrorist and Proliferation Financing (CTPF) framework, with effective and proportionate policies, procedures, controls, guidance, and training to prevent, detect, and respond to financial crime risks. • Act as Deputy MLRO for Great Britain and any other future licences, deputising in the MLRO’s absence and ensuring continuity of statutory reporting obligations and day to day financial crime oversight. • Assess internal disclosures and determine whether there is knowledge or suspicion of money laundering, terrorist financing, or proliferation financing and escalate to the MLRO or law enforcement accordingly. • Support with the ongoing development of the Compliance technical roadmap. • Contribute where appropriate to the Complaints and Escalations process, which sits within the Regulatory Compliance team, ensuring any technical compliance investigations are conducted in a timely manner. • Work closely with the Compliance Manager & MLRO to coordinate and prepare for regulatory inspections, internal audits, and external assurance engagements. • Draft compliance development and bug tickets via clickup and work closely with technical specialists to agree satisfactory acceptance criteria for projects. • Draft and deliver technical compliance reports on new and emergent RTS (and equivalent) regulations, and recommend development actions to mitigate any new risks or requirements. • Own the mapping of technical regulatory requirements, including UKGC Remote Technical Standards and equivalent international standards, into clear product and engineering requirements, ensuring these are embedded through design, development, testing, and release management. • Lead ongoing testing and assurance of key technical controls such as self-exclusion, time outs, reality checks, deposit limits, game fairness and RTP configurations, KYC and customer due diligence flows, and transaction monitoring rules. • Collaborate with the Product team and Compliance Manager to support project management and delivery of compliance strategies and roadmaps. • Support the oversight of critical third parties, including platform providers, game studios, KYC and payments vendors, and safer gambling tools, ensuring that technical and financial crime controls remain effective on an end-to-end basis and that regulatory requirements are reflected in operational arrangements. • Support incident management and post incident reviews where technical failures have actual or potential regulatory, financial crime, or customer harm implications, and ensure remedial actions are identified, prioritised, and tracked to completion. • Maintain an accurate and up to date Games Register for all regulated markets, including responsibility for submitting and updating game information with relevant regulators, such as via the UK Gambling Commission’s eServices portal. • Ensure that all new game launches, game changes, and game withdrawals are correctly reflected in the Games Register and aligned with internal approval processes, contractual permissions, and applicable regulatory requirements. • Own and oversee adherence to the Group’s Remote Software Audit Policy, ensuring that required testing, certifications, and periodic audits are planned, completed, and evidenced in line with regulatory expectations. • Act as the primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders in relation to game approvals, game certification, and software audit activity, including coordination with platform providers, game studios, test labs, and regulators where appropriate. • Support the MLRO with preparing quarterly and annual MLRO reports for the board, supporting strong oversight and continuous improvement of the group’s financial crime framework. • Assist the MLRO with oversight of suspicious activity reporting across jurisdictions, including the quality and timeliness of SARs, DAMLs, and equivalent submissions to FIUs. • Support the Player Protection Manager in the development, maintenance, and delivery of effective financial crime training materials, ensuring all employees understand their responsibilities in identifying and reporting suspicious activity. • Act as an escalation point for compliance analysts and nominated officers on complex or sensitive cases involving potential money laundering or other forms of illicit activity. • Undertake ad hoc tasks and projects as reasonably requested by the Head of Compliance. These may include regulatory remediation work, interviews, panel contributions, roundtable participation, or other cross-functional initiatives. Essential Skills • Proven experience in a compliance role within the regulated gambling sector, with demonstrable AML experience. • A strong understanding of either the Gambling Commission of Great Britain regulatory frameworks, including relevant legislation, guidance, and best practice standards. • Working knowledge of the Proceeds of Crime Act, the Money Laundering Regulations, the Terrorism Act, and relevant guidance. • Proven ability to manage complex casework and make proportionate, risk-based decisions under pressure. • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present information clearly, accurately, and with appropriate nuance for different audiences. • Strong stakeholder management capabilities, with prior experience in delivering cross-functional projects. • High level of organisation and time management, with the ability to balance multiple competing priorities across jurisdictions and disciplines. • Adaptability to change and comfort working in a fast-paced, high-growth environment where commercial and regulatory priorities evolve rapidly. • Proficient in Microsoft Office tools and confident handling data-driven decision making and reporting. • A recognised AML qualification (e.g. ICA or equivalent) is highly desirable.

items.title: Operational Excellence & Incident Response Manager, Predictions Markets
items.description: About us Crypto.com is building the regulated home for prediction markets and derivatives in the United States. Through Crypto.com Derivatives North America and OG.com we operate a CFTC-designated contract market and a registered clearinghouse. OG.com Prediction Markets lists event contracts on sports, politics, economics, culture, and crypto, including single-event contracts and combos. The problem you'll solve It's Saturday night in the US. A partner broker messages: their customers' orders are stuck, and their support queue is filling up. You do not yet know if it is our gateway, their routing, the market data feed, or the settlement logic. People who can fix it are in the US, in Asia, or asleep. Today, whoever sees the message first owns it. That is the gap. You are the single owner of every production incident that touches OG.com Prediction Markets, the exchange, the clearinghouse, or our partner brokers, from the first alert to the final review. You do not write the fix. You decide who does, within minutes. You keep every affected partner current. You make the risk call on what happens in the next 20 minutes, the next 3 hours, and on Monday morning. Root cause is identified in the first 30 minutes. An issue does not sit open for four hours. A platform failure usually hits many partners at once, not one. You run that room. You report to the SVP of Product. You do not have a team on day one. Within 6 to 12 months, a person who is good at this builds the rotation and owns the partner relationships that come with it. What you decide: severity, who gets paged, the live timeline, every partner update while the incident is open, and the recommendation to pause, halt, cancel, or keep trading. The on-call approver approves a pause or halt. Exchange Operations owns the listing and the settlement call. Engineering owns the code. Life @ Crypto.com Empowered to think big. Try new opportunities while working with a talented, ambitious and supportive team. Transformational and proactive working environment. Empower employees to find thoughtful and innovative solutions. Growth from within. We help to develop new skill-sets that would impact the shaping of your personal and professional growth. Work Culture. Our colleagues are some of the best in the industry; we are all here to help and support one another. One cohesive team. Engage stakeholders to achieve our ultimate goal - Cryptocurrency in every wallet. Work Flexibility Adoption. Flexi-work hour and hybrid set-up Aspire career alternatives through us - our internal mobility program offers employees a new scope. Are you ready to kickstart your future with us? Benefits Competitive salary Attractive annual leave entitlement including: birthday, work anniversary 401(k) plan with employer match Eligible for company-sponsored group health, dental, vision, and life/disability insurance Work Flexibility Adoption. Flexi-work hour and hybrid set-up Aspire career alternatives through us. Our internal mobility program can offer employees a diverse scope. Our Crypto.com benefits packages vary depending on region requirements, you can learn more from our talent acquisition team. Our vision is simple: Cryptocurrency in Every Wallet™. Built on a foundation of security, privacy, and compliance, Crypto.com is committed to accelerating the adoption of cryptocurrency through innovation and empowering the next generation of builders, creators, and entrepreneurs to develop a fairer and more equitable digital ecosystem. Learn more at https://crypto.com. Crypto.com is an equal opportunities employer and we are committed to creating an environment where opportunities are presented to everyone in a fair and transparent way. Crypto.com values diversity and inclusion, seeking candidates with a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills that complement and strengthen our team. items.title: Senior Product Designer
items.description: Help Us Build The Future of Travel At Airalo, we're making it easier for people to stay connected wherever they travel. As the world's first eSIM store, we help millions of travelers access affordable mobile data in 200+ countries and regions around the world. Today, we're a team of 400+ people across 60+ countries, building a product used by travelers every day. We've grown quickly, but we've worked hard to keep what matters: trust, ownership, and the freedom for people to do great work without unnecessary layers or bureaucracy. We're fully remote by design, genuinely global, and united by a shared mission to make travel simpler for everyone. Your Next Destination Location: Remote, anywhere in Spain or the UK. Contract: Spain: Full-time, permanent contrato indefinido via Deel (our employer of record in Spain) UK: Full-time, permanent Benefits: Learn more about our benefits here in this link - https://airalo-public.notion.site/Benefits-25396a97ffca81fb9bc1f0be479f1be3?pvs=74 Languages: English is our main working language day to day, so you'll need to be comfortable communicating in it both in meetings and async. Curious what it's actually like to work at Airalo? items.title: Strategic Pursuits Lead, DACH
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the Role As a Strategic Pursuits Lead at Anthropic, you will operate as an elite individual contributor running our largest and most complex enterprise pursuits end-to-end. You will serve as the strategic quarterback for high-stakes engagements with Fortune 100 companies and global institutions, owning the C-suite relationships and discussions each pursuit demands while working hand in hand with the account team and field leadership who own the account. That ownership is an and, not an or, and the pursuit only works when both are true. You will coordinate across product, research, partnerships, legal, and executive leadership, and architect bespoke solutions that unlock transformational business value. When the agreement is signed, you will hand the account back in a healthy state, with the account team positioned to execute what was signed and a playbook behind you. This role reports directly to the Head of Strategic Pursuits. Responsibilities Lead end-to-end orchestration of Anthropic’s most strategic and complex enterprise pursuits. Own the C-suite relationships and discussions on each pursuit, in full partnership with the account team and field leadership who own the account Design and execute sophisticated account strategies that position Claude as mission-critical infrastructure for enterprise transformation Navigate intricate multi-stakeholder decision processes across technical, business, legal, security, and procurement functions Partner with product and research teams to shape custom solutions and influence roadmap priorities for strategic accounts Coordinate cross-functional pursuit resources including sales, partnerships, technical specialists, and executive sponsors Develop innovative commercial structures, deployment models, and partnership frameworks for complex strategic engagements Drive competitive differentiation in head-to-head pursuits against established technology incumbents Codify what works into playbooks and constructs the broader commercial organization can reuse, and plan every pursuit's hand back so the account team is set up to deliver what was signed Represent Anthropic in high-stakes negotiations and executive forums with global business leaders You may be a good fit if you have 15+ years of progressive experience in enterprise technology, with at least 7+ years personally leading strategic deals or major account pursuits in the DACH region Proven track record of closing multiple enterprise technology deals with Fortune 100 companies as the primary deal owner Deep expertise in complex B2B sales cycles involving C-suite engagement, technical validation, and cross-functional coordination Demonstrated ability to architect sophisticated solutions that address complex enterprise requirements Strong understanding of enterprise AI/ML deployment models, cloud infrastructure, and API integration patterns Exceptional strategic thinking with the ability to synthesize business, technical, and competitive dynamics Outstanding executive presence and ability to build trust with C-level stakeholders Experience navigating Fortune 500 procurement, legal, security, and compliance processes Track record of winning in highly competitive, must-win pursuit scenarios Nice to have: Experience in management consulting (MBB) or strategic advisory roles Technical background or strong fluency in AI/ML technologies Experience with global systems integrator relationships and complex partner ecosystems International deal experience across multiple regions The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: €380.000 — €605.000 EUR Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.
